Some games are settled by one big moment. This one had a second act.

On August 16, 2026, at Mazda Stadium, the Hanshin Tigers took the lead in the first inning. Teruaki Sato hit a two-run home run to center field, putting Hanshin ahead 2-0.

But a two-run lead is not the same as a finished game.

Hiroshima came back in the fifth inning. Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run, cutting the gap to 2-1. It was Hiroshima’s only run of the night, but it brought the home team within reach.

Hanshin’s starting pitcher, Ihara, helped keep his team in front. He worked five innings, allowed two hits, and gave up one run. Even after Hiroshima’s home run, Hanshin held the lead.

Then the visitors added runs in the seventh and eighth innings. Timely hits gave Hanshin more room, turning the close 2-1 game into a one-sided finish.

The final score was Hiroshima 1, Hanshin 8.

【Point One】
Look at the scoring in two parts. Sato’s home run created the first advantage, but Hiroshima’s fifth-inning response narrowed the margin again. Hanshin then answered in the seventh and eighth, when Seishiro Sakamoto and pinch-hitter Fushimi delivered timely hits. The decisive margin came from that second push, not the opening home run alone.

【Point Two】
The safest pitching conclusion is a narrow one. Ihara gave Hanshin five innings, allowing two hits and one run, while Hiroshima’s only scoring play was Montero’s solo home run. That supports credit for Ihara’s work. But no reliever-by-reliever account is confirmed here, so the record does not support calling the entire pitching performance a complete shutdown.
